title: How To Register And Fund Your MTI Account

asr.full_text: How to register and fund your Mirror Trading International account You will need the referral link of the person who invited you to join Mirror Trading International It will look something like this Click on that link and you will be taken to the registration screen Your sponsor's username will be displayed in the sponsor information section Next you'll see that auto-placement is displayed Please check with your sponsor weather you should select the Left or Right hand position. If you don't make a selection, you will automatically go into your sponsor's Team Leg. Enter a username – the system will tell you if the user name is available – and a password Fill-in your personal information – Name, surname, email address, a valid mobile number, and then choose your country from the drop-down list. Read the terms and conditions and then click I have read and accepted the terms and conditions. Once you have done this click on the register button. A screen will come up with a confirmation message which will confirm your login details. You will also receive an email from mirror trading international, confirming your registration. If you found this email in your spam folder, you can inform your system that it is not spam and you will be able to receive other emails from the company. Now that you have your login details, please log in to the BACK office at mymticlub.com. Then click on the Profile button in the menu on the left. Please update your personal details and upload your proof of identity. Once you have done this, you can click the Update button. Adding funds to your Meritrading International pool account. Click on the Wallet section on the left. A roll-down will appear. Click on the wallet section on the left. A rolledown will appear, click on Add Funds. The Payment Information screen will appear. You can either scan the QR code or carefully copy the Bitcoin address to your wallet. Make the payment by sending the bitcoin. Remember some wallets require you to verify the payment, via email. Fill in the details. The exact amount of bitcoin you sent. Enter the blockchain transaction ID, or Tx ID. Upload proof of payment screenshot. Click submit. Once the Admin has confirmed your Bitcoin transfer. It will appear in your trading account. In this case your dashboard will confirm that you are a paid member. However in some circumstances your balance may be in the Activation Wallet. If your Bitcoin is in your Activation Wallet then click on the Add Funds To Pool or click on pool account in the menu on the left and the roll down and click Add Funds To Pool. The amount of Bitcoin you want to transfer from your activation wallet will show, and all you need to do is click on submit. Go back to your dashboard, and confirm that your Bitcoin is now in the trading account, and that your status says paid member. Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades. You can also log in to your backice to see these results and your statements. Click on the view option to see your daily statement. That is your account and how to see the results from daily trading. Should you wish to refer your friends you can send them your registration link or you can help them register by clicking on the downstream registration link.

Fill-in your personal information – Name, surname, email address, a valid mobile number
Please update your personal details and upload your proof of identity.

textual.context: Instructional account-registration walkthrough; the supplied records do not establish whether the speaker is promoting, warning about, or reporting the service.
textual.potential_relevance: The source links a referral-based registration process and submission of personal and identity information to opening the named trading account, requiring later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish how the information is handled, whether the service is legitimate, or whether any harm occurred.

textual.observation: The source instructs viewers to fund the account by sending Bitcoin to a displayed wallet destination, submitting the transaction ID and payment proof, and confirming paid-member status in the trading account.

your dashboard will confirm that you are a paid member.

textual.context: Instructional funding walkthrough that describes Bitcoin transfer and payment verification; no explicit guarantee of profit or return is stated in the supplied records.
textual.potential_relevance: The source directly ties a requested cryptocurrency transfer and submission of transaction evidence to paid-member status and placement of funds in a trading account, requiring later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the recipient's identity, transaction outcome, investment performance, or whether the account or funding process is legitimate.

visual.observation: The signup and profile screens visibly request a username and password, first and last name, email address, mobile number, address, date of birth, gender, ID number, and uploaded proof.
visual.context: Account-registration and profile-completion screens; a Terms and Conditions acceptance control is also visible.
visual.potential_relevance: The workflow links collection of contact and identity information, including ID and proof, to access to a bitcoin-linked account and funding interface.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish whether the information was submitted, how it would be used, or whether any identity was verified.

visual.observation: A "Payment Information" screen displays a Bitcoin QR code, a wallet address string, a BTC amount field, a transaction-ID field, an upload control for proof of payment, and a "Submit" button.
visual.context: The payment step is shown inside a "Back Office" interface as part of the account workflow.
visual.potential_relevance: The screen explicitly connects a requested cryptocurrency transfer and transaction-proof submission to account funding or participation in the displayed service.
visual.limitations: The samples do not establish whether the QR code was scanned, whether a transaction occurred or was confirmed, who controlled the destination, or what happened afterward.

visual.observation: The dashboard shows an activation wallet balance of 0.01340000 BTC and a trading pool balance of 0 BTC; a subsequent screen titled "Add Funds To Trading Pool" shows the same BTC amount prefilled with a "Submit" control.
visual.context: This appears as a sequential account-dashboard and funding workflow; the exact relationship between the balances is not otherwise explained in the sampled frames.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible sequence moves from an activation balance to an additional instruction to submit funds into a trading pool, showing a conditional funding step tied to account use.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish whether the second submission occurred, whether funds moved, or whether the displayed balances were accurate.

visual.observation: The account dashboard and trading-bonus report display "Trading Bonuses," percentage figures in remarks, and multiple entries marked "Paid."
visual.context: These labels appear within an account dashboard and bonus-report interface alongside the BTC funding workflow.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible paid-bonus records and percentage-based remarks present a return or bonus claim in the same account flow that includes cryptocurrency funding and trading-pool actions.
visual.limitations: The samples do not establish that any payout occurred, that the entries were genuine, or that the bonuses were caused by a particular deposit or action.

textual_context_notes.observation: The source describes receiving statements about trading results rather than stating a guaranteed return.

evidence.quote: Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

visual_context_notes.observation: The sequence is framed as account-registration and funding guidance, with a title referring to registering and funding an MTI account and a closing "Join now" screen.
A Terms and Conditions panel with an acceptance control is visible before registration.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it invites its audience to register for a named trading account and explicitly prompts them to join. It instructs participants to send Bitcoin, submit a transaction ID and payment proof, and move an activation-wallet balance into a trading pool. It also requests identity information and displays paid percentage-based trading bonuses, although the available video evidence does not establish that any transaction, payout, identity verification, or displayed result was completed or genuine.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The video presents participation in a Bitcoin-funded trading pool and links that participation to trading results and displayed trading bonuses. The evidence supports a pool or managed-trading return relationship, while it does not establish that any displayed bonus was actually paid or caused by a particular transfer.
